```{r}
unexpected_indispo_ENTSOE_data  <- bout_indispo_ENTSOE_data %>% 
  filter(businesstype=='Unplanned outage') %>% 
  ungroup()%>% 
  #exclude events which publication delay is greater than 24 hours
  mutate(lapse = difftime(datetime_debut, datetime_pub, units = "hours")) %>%

  mutate(year = year(datetime_debut))

       y = "Frequency") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
# Charger le package patchwork pour combiner les graphiques
library(patchwork)
library(cowplot)
library(gridExtra)
library(grid)
library(latex2exp)
library(ggplot2)

non_duplicated_indispo$year <- year(non_duplicated_indispo$electricity_delivery_date)


plot_data <- non_duplicated_indispo %>% 
  select(electricity_delivery_date, Unavailable.Capacity, plant_type, year) %>% 
  group_by(year, plant_type) %>% 
  summarise(Unavailable.Capacity.mean = mean(as.numeric(Unavailable.Capacity)),
         n_indispo = n()) 

# Premier graphique: Unavailable Capacity par Fuel Type
plot1 <- ggplot() +
  geom_bar(data = plot_data, aes(x = as.factor(year), y = Unavailable.Capacity.mean, fill = plant_type), alpha=0.4,
           stat = "identity", position = "dodge") +
  
  geom_bar(data = updated_plot_data, aes(x = as.factor(year), y = real_unavailability.mean, fill = plant_type), 
           stat = "identity", position = "dodge") +
  
  labs(x = 'Date de publication', y = "Unavailable Capacity") +
  theme_minimal()

custom_legend <- cowplot::get_legend(plot1)

plot1 <-plot1 +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
  
# Deuxième graphique: Nombre d'indisponibilités (n_indispo)
plot2 <- ggplot() +
  geom_bar(data = plot_data, aes(x = as.factor(year), y = -n_indispo, fill = plant_type), alpha=0.4, 
           stat = "identity", position = "dodge") +
  geom_bar(data = updated_plot_data, aes(x = as.factor(year), y = -n_indispo, fill = plant_type), 
           stat = "identity", position = "dodge") +
  labs(y = "Nombre d\'indisponibilités") +
  theme_minimal()+
  theme(axis.title.x = element_blank(), # Désactiver le titre de l'axe des x
        axis.text.x = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "none")  # Désactiver les ticks de l'axe des x
  # Ajouter un titre personnalisé comme annotation
  #+annotate("text", x = Inf, y = -Inf, label = "Number of Power Outages", 
           #hjust = 1.4, vjust = -1.5, size = 5)
# Assembler les deux graphiques verticalement avec patchwork
combined_plot <- plot1 / plot2 #+ draw_plot(custom_legend, x = 0.8, y = 0.5, width = 0.2, height = 0.5)
# Combine the grid with the legend
final_plot <- plot_grid(combined_plot, custom_legend ,
                        ncol = 2, rel_heights = c(1, 0.1))



# Afficher le graphique combiné
final_plot

```

Deuxième graphique avec la méthode de prévision par random forest

```{r}

real_plot_pred_data <- real_indispo_rf %>%
```

On combine toutes les informations sur un même graphique


```{r}

# Premier graphique: Unavailable Capacity par Fuel Type
plot1 <- ggplot() +
  geom_bar(data = plot_data, aes(x = as.factor(year), y = Unavailable.Capacity.mean, fill = plant_type), alpha=0.4,
           stat = "identity", position = "dodge") +
  
  geom_bar(data = updated_plot_data, aes(x = as.factor(year), y = real_unavailability.mean, fill = plant_type), 
           stat = "identity", position = "dodge",alpha=0.8, color= 'black' ) 
plot1 <- plot1 +
  geom_point(data= real_plot_pred_data, mapping = aes(x = as.factor(year), y = -predicted_real_unavailability.mean, color = plant_type), size = 3, position = position_dodge(width = 0.85)) +  
  # Ajouter des points pour la moyenne et espacer
  geom_linerange(data= real_plot_pred_data, 
                 aes(x= as.factor(year), 
      ymin = 0, ymax = -predicted_real_unavailability.mean, color = plant_type), 
                 size = 1,
                 position = position_dodge(width = 0.85)) + 
    labs(x = 'Date de publication', y = "Unavailable Capacity") +
  theme_minimal()

custom_legend <- cowplot::get_legend(plot1)

plot1 <-plot1 +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
  
# Deuxième graphique: Nombre d'indisponibilités (n_indispo)
plot2 <- ggplot() +
  geom_bar(data = plot_data, aes(x = as.factor(year), y = -n_indispo, fill = plant_type), alpha=0.4, 
           stat = "identity", position = "dodge") +
  geom_bar(data = updated_plot_data, aes(x = as.factor(year), y = -n_indispo, fill = plant_type), 
           stat = "identity", position = "dodge",alpha=0.8, color= 'black') +
  labs(y = "Nombre d\'indisponibilités") +
  theme_minimal() # Désactiver les ticks de l'axe des x


plot2 <- plot2 +
  geom_point(data= real_plot_pred_data, mapping = aes(x = as.factor(year), y = -n_indispo, color = plant_type), size = 3, position = position_dodge(width = 0.85)) +  
  # Ajouter des points pour la moyenne et espacer
  geom_linerange(data= real_plot_pred_data, 
                 aes(x= as.factor(year), 
      ymin = 0, ymax = -n_indispo, color = plant_type), 
                 size = 1,
                 position = position_dodge(width = 0.85)) + 
  
  theme_minimal()+
  theme(axis.title.x = element_blank(), # Désactiver le titre de l'axe des x
        axis.text.x = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "none") 

  # Ajouter un titre personnalisé comme annotation
  #+annotate("text", x = Inf, y = -Inf, label = "Number of Power Outages", 
           #hjust = 1.4, vjust = -1.5, size = 5)
# Assembler les deux graphiques verticalement avec patchwork
combined_plot <- plot1 / plot2 #+ draw_plot(custom_legend, x = 0.8, y = 0.5, width = 0.2, height = 0.5)
# Combine the grid with the legend
final_plot <- plot_grid(combined_plot, custom_legend ,
                        ncol = 2, rel_heights = c(1, 0.1))



# Afficher le graphique combiné
final_plot


```

Je peux faire une légende des formes

On plotte maintenant les séries en question


```{r}


my_plot <- ggplot(data = complete_data) +
  geom_line(aes(x = datetime, y = Unavailable.Capacity, color = "Declared Unavailability")) +
  geom_line(aes(x = datetime, y = real_unavailability, color = "Real Unavailability")) +
  geom_line(aes(x = datetime, y = nuclear_real_unavailability, color = "Nuclear Real Unavailability")) +
  geom_line(aes(x = datetime, y = -predicted_real_unavailability, color = "Predicted Real Unavailability")) +
  labs(
    x = 'Electricity delivery date',
    y = "Unavailable Capacity (in MW)",
    title = "Power Outages News Shock",
    color = "Legend"  # Label for the legend
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

my_plot

```



Those figures are to be compared with the total capacity installed in Spain that is between 120 (ENTSOE platform data for 2024) and 150 GW (sum of IIP installed capacity).
The daily generation of energy is about 80 GWh.
The hourly generation power ranges between 20 GW at the night without wind and 40 GW during the day
(not very clear on the entsoe website)

Thus, the kind of shocks that we are looking at are in magnitude of 500 MW to 2GW that is at most 2% of electricity generation.

Nota bene: it could depend on whether this plant was supposed to generate electricity, maybe get the generation schedule, to deduce which have low marginal cost,
maybe it depends from fuel type and whether or not 'pilotable'

This magnitude is rather small.
Yet, we expect that the price setting mechanism of marginal pricing will have a substantial (and maybe discontinuous) impact on prices by forcing a new high-cost unit to produce on the market.

# Renewable intermittence shock serie

Load associated data
```{r}

              'renewable_forecasts.parquet')
```

Get some summary statistics

```{r}
# some summary stat
describe(renewable_shock_series)
```



Plot the difference between the two graphs

```{r}
date_time_string <- "2021/01/07 00:00:00"

# Convert to POSIXct
posixct_date_time <- as.POSIXct(date_time_string, format = "%Y/%m/%d %H:%M:%S")

renewable_shock_first_week <- renewable_shock_series%>% 
  rename(datetime =`__index_level_0__`) %>% 
  filter(datetime < posixct_date_time )

my_plot <- ggplot(data =renewable_shock_first_week)+
  geom_line(aes(x =datetime , y = Intraday_Fore_Solar, color="Intraday Solar")) +
geom_line(aes(x =datetime , y = Fore_Solar, color="Day Before Solar")) +
  geom_line(aes(x =datetime , y = Intraday_Fore_Wind, color="Intraday Wind")) +
  geom_line(aes(x =datetime , y = Fore_Wind, color="Day Before Wind")) +
  labs(x= 'Electricity delivery date', y = "Difference between the two predictions", 
       title = "Intermittence uncertainty news shock") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Intraday Solar" = "darkblue", "Day Before Solar" = "blue", "Intraday Wind" = "darkgreen", "Day Before Wind" = "lightgreen")) +
  theme_minimal()

my_plot
```

The 7 auctions can give rise to different price series.

Let's look at it first on a single day window

```{r}
price_data_2021_09_09 <- price_data %>% 
  filter(year=='2021' & month=='6' & day == '24')

my_plot <- ggplot(price_data_2021_09_09, aes(x =datetime , y = price, color= auction)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x= 'Date', y = "Price (in €)", 
       title = "Electricty price series on the auction intra-day market") +
  theme_minimal()

my_plot
```
